correctness.rationale: The ideal-count recurrence N_h=1+N_(h-1)^2 gives 2,5,26,677. Eight leaves are VC-shattered, forcing Ldim>=8. For every first query in height three, the negative branch at depth 0/1/2 has 1/27/157 concepts, with log bounds 0/4/7, and every leaf-positive branch is the disjoint-domain product of height-0, -1 and -2 ideal classes, of dimensions 1+2+4=7. Standard product additivity follows from the Littlestone recurrence. The upper bound is 8 and all h<=2 have matching cardinality upper bounds. Independently implemented exact poset-deletion and membership-version-space algorithms agree on all four classes.

value.rationale: The exact dimension determines the optimal realizable worst-case mistake budget of a natural 15-variable hierarchical Horn concept class; 677 hypotheses permit nine mistakes by counting but the structure reduces this to eight. It is the minimal height in the canonical perfect-binary sequence at which entropy ceases to predict the correct online dimension, furnishing a mathematically motivated finite benchmark and clear structural obstruction, rather than an arbitrary selected instance or an exercise in recomputing a known table. The restricted value is not advertised as an all-height theorem.
